Thanks again for the demo today — great to see Redwood's streaming in action. A couple of follow-ups from our engineering and product teams:

- Our product goal is <250ms time-to-first-token (TTFT) for the majority of customer-facing flows (P50 target), with P95 ideally <600ms.
- We expect sustained concurrency of ~800-1200 active users during peak promotions (concurrency = simultaneous interactive sessions).
- We need streaming over SSE (WebSockets is optional) with first chunk delivered as quickly as possible and subsequent chunk cadence of ~100-300ms for progressive rendering.

Could you confirm if these targets are achievable on a dedicated deployment and what trade-offs we should expect (quantization, batching, prefix cache warm-up)? Also, can you send a simple test plan so our infra team can run a reproducible TTFT run?

Adding some engineering specifics from the SE side — hi Tom / Priya. A few notes to make the TTFT runs comparable across environments: 

Measurement guidance:
- Measure TTFT from the client-side (time from request sent to first byte of application payload). Report both P50 and P95.
- Include cold start and warm start scenarios (cache cold, and with warmed prefix/KV cache). Warm starts typically shave 50–200ms depending on prefix reuse.
- Track tokenization time; different client tokenizers can add 10–40ms. We recommend using the same tokenizer code for both test and production.

Performance knobs and expectations:
- Batch size: continuous batching helps throughput but may add queuing latency. For strict TTFT, keep batching small (or prefer single-request low-latency paths).
- Quantization: 4-bit (Q4) often provides good cost/perf; FP16 gives best latency but higher memory. We'll recommend quant profiles based on your model.
- SSE vs WebSocket: both supported. SSE has simpler client integration; WebSocket slightly reduces per-connection overhead at very high concurrency.

Suggested test profile (we included in the spreadsheet):
- Short run: 10-minute warm-up + 10-minute measurement at target concurrency (800, 1,000, 1,200)
- Long run: 1-hour ramp to 1,200 then steady-state 30 minutes (for peaking behavior)

I'll be available next Tue/Wed 10am–2pm PT to run a joint test and tune parameters.

-Rishi
